claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my child Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know about Alex!

To help determine your eligibility, could you please tell me how old Alex is?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Now I have a few more questions to help determine your eligibility.

Are you responsible for Alex's care? This means Alex lives with you, or you contribute at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards their upkeep each week.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for confirming that.

Could you tell me where you and Alex live? Specifically, are you living in the United Kingdom (England, Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, we live in England - in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Lovely, thank you. Just a couple more questions.

Is Alex currently in full-time education or approved training, or are they simply below school-leaving age (under 16)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is only 8, so they're just in primary school - well below the school-leaving age.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you.

One more question: Are you (or your partner, if applicable) subject to immigration control, or do you have any restrictions on your stay in the UK that might affect your access to public funds?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, we don't have any immigration restrictions - I'm a British citizen and have full access to public funds.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all that information. Based on what you've told me, I have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm pleased to tell you that **you appear to be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of the key reasons:

- ✅ **Alex qualifies as a child** – At 8 years old, Alex is well below the school-leaving age of 16
- ✅ **You are responsible for Alex** – Alex lives with you
- ✅ **You live in the UK** – You're residing in England (Manchester)
- ✅ **No immigration restrictions** – As a British citizen, you have full access to public funds

**Next steps:** You can apply for Child Benefit online through the official government website, or by post using the Child Benefit claim form (CH2).

Please note that if you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may have to pay back some or all of your Child Benefit through the High Income Child Benefit Charge. However, it can still be worth claiming to protect your National Insurance record and ensure your child gets a National Insurance number automatically at 16.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
